title: Equivariant Diffusion for Molecule Generation in 3D
layout_note: A 2x2 commutative square: noisy point cloud and its rotated copy in the top row, molecule and its rotated copy in the bottom row; rotation arrows run across each row and diffuse/denoise arrow pairs run down each column, with an equation under the bottom row.
grouping: No containers or panel letters; the four drawings are placed on a grid and tied only by the arrows. Element type is coded by fill colour, the same in all four drawings (grey, pink, blue, white).
shapes_depth: Atoms are flat filled circles with thick black outlines, hydrogen-like atoms smaller and white; bonds are thick black lines. The noisy states are the same circles scattered without bonds. Horizontal arrows are solid black with a bold R and a small dashed circular-arrow rotation glyph above; vertical arrows are dashed curved pairs (one up, one down) labelled with italic math and the words diffuse and denoise.
proposed_highlight: No module is drawn; the property is the message: the bottom row ends in the equation p(x,h) = p(Rx,h), with the equals sign placed between the two columns.
lesson: State an equivariance claim as a commutative square: the object and its noised version in one column, their rotated copies in the other, rotation arrows across, diffuse/denoise arrows down, and the invariance equation set under the bottom row with '=' between the columns.
notes: Venue from the PDF footer ('Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning ... PMLR 162, 2022'; venue_source: pdf).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: architecture other: concept teaser showing equivariance, no network drawn

core.what: an equivariance property drawn as a 2 x 2 commutative square on toy molecules: noisy atom clouds on the top row, molecules on the bottom row, original on the left and rotated by R on the right, ending in p(x,h) = p(Rx,h) with the equals sign between the columns

relations.form: the method acts on a small drawn molecule (a ring of grey atoms with red, blue and white substituents) and its noised version, a scatter of the same coloured circles without bonds
the two columns face each other across horizontal 'R' arrows with a small rotation icon, and the bottom row closes with p(x,h) = p(Rx,h), the equals sign centred between the columns
each column has a pair of opposed dashed curved arrows between the rows, 'diffuse' q(z_T,...|x,h) upward and 'denoise' p(x,h,...|z_T) downward

channels.colour: atom type only: grey, red, blue and white circles keep their colours from the molecule into the noise cloud and across the rotation; no colour is used for modules
channels.shape: circle = atom, size distinguishing heavy atoms from hydrogens; bond lines exist only in the clean molecules
channels.line: solid arrows = the rotation R, dashed curved arrows = the stochastic diffuse/denoise processes
channels.frame: none; the four states sit at the corners of the square

quality.strengths: The property itself is the geometry: two columns related by R, two rows related by diffusion, and the equality placed exactly between the column ends; data are drawn as molecules and atom clouds with consistent atom colours; no module boxes compete with the message, and every arrow is short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: Process names are written as typeset distributions beside the arrows rather than short names; the rotation icon is tiny and the top-right cloud is hard to check as a rotation of the top-left one; the claim is only stated for the bottom row, so the top row's role (that the noise process is also equivariant) is left implicit.

insights.structure: A 2 x 2 commutative square with no containers: noisy atom clouds in the top row, molecules in the bottom row, the left column original and the right column rotated.
insights.data: Atoms are flat filled circles with thick black outlines coloured by element (grey, pink, blue, small white), bonds are thick black lines, and the noisy states are the same circles scattered without bonds.
insights.emphasis: The bottom row ends in the equation p(x,h) = p(Rx,h) with the equals sign placed exactly between the two columns, so the property itself is the message.
insights.flow: Horizontal solid arrows labelled R with a dashed rotation glyph run across each row; between rows each column has a dashed curved pair of arrows labelled 'diffuse' with q(...) and 'denoise' with p(...).
